HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Long lens down the length of the Summit table in a dark timber hall, the king on a low dais at the far end, crowned, leaning forward with interest toward the Southern Commander who sits nearest him, gesturing at a map on the table. Every other head turns to them. In the sharp near foreground, at the foot of the table, Yeon Gesomun sits alone and last, beside the clerk’s inkstone, a teacup at his lips, eyes over its rim fixed on the king. Crow-stamped ring-pommel swords lie on the table before each seat except his. One hard window shaft falls on the king and the South; Yeon is lit only by a small oil lamp at his elbow, warm from the side. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = gesomun, SECOND face = yeongnyu, THIRD face = southcmd; its bottom row is the only sword design. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. YEON GESOMUN — Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Colour #d0362f. KING YOUNGRYU — Crown: Goguryeo gold crown: a gold band crowded with upright flame and branch sprays hung with small round gold spangles; at court the king may instead wear the tall silk cap of the king on the costume chart. Colour #a83b34. SON DAEHA Colour #c46b3a. PLACE Pyongyang (평양성) — attached board /pl_pyongyang_city.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
